subject: Latency spike + failover: us-west-2 impacting OrbitAI
messages:
From: Nina Rao <nina@orbitai.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@orbitai.com
Date: 2026-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production latency spike -> failover to us-east causing 5xxs

Hi Lauren,

We're seeing a severe spike in end-to-end latency from our customers in the Pacific region starting ~08:45 PST. A subset of requests are failing with 502/504, and our telemetry shows a large fraction of production traffic shifted to us-east-1 after what looks like an AZ-level network degradation in us-west-2.

Impact:~
- 30% increase in p95 latency for inference calls for the last 30m
- Error rate up from 0.3% -> ~4.8% for public API keys
- Several high-volume customers reporting dropped sessions

I've attached a quick latency snapshot and a CSV with traffic counts. We're in the middle of a run for a major pre-launch traffic window, so this is urgent. Please escalate and advise immediate mitigations.

Nina Rao
CTO, OrbitAI

Attachments: latency-snapshot-20260214.png, traffic-metrics-20260214.csv
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: nina@orbitai.com
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike -> failover to us-east causing 5xxs

Nina — thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments. We're escalating to the on-call infra and network teams now. Immediate actions I'm initiating:

1) Force-route high-priority OrbitAI traffic to our us-east-1 standby pool for the next 30m while we stabilize us-west-2.
2) Temporarily raise rate limits on dedicated routes for OrbitAI to avoid backpressure-induced 5xxs.
3) Collect full request traces and KV-cache hit rates for the last 60m (will share).

Marcus is on routing and will send the change diff. Sean will track the customer comms and any SLO/credit asks. Evelyn, looping you as this may need exec attention (OrbitAI is a strategic account / ORB-4523).

I'll confirm once forced routing is live.

—Lauren
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: nina@orbitai.com, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike -> failover to us-east causing 5xxs

Lauren — routing change applied at 09:52 PST.

Summary of technical changes:
- Updated routing policy: orbitai-prod route priority bumped to prefer us-east-1 (weight 80) with graceful drain of us-west-2 nodes.
- Increased concurrent request cap for OrbitAI dedicated pool from 1200 -> 1800 for 2 hours.
- Added path pinning for 20% of sessions to maintain affinity while we rebuild hot KV caches.

Attached: routing-change-diff.patch and a small CSV with per-AZ reject rates. Preliminary metrics show p95 latency returning toward baseline in the last 10 minutes.

On Tue, Feb 14, 2026 at 09:12 AM Nina Rao <nina@orbitai.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a severe spike in end-to-end latency from our customers in the Pacific region starting ~08:45 PST.
> ...

—Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: routing-change-diff.patch
From: CloudIntegrate Support <aws-partner@cloudintegrate.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: nina@orbitai.com
Date: 2026-02-14T12:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Production latency spike / AZ network degradation (us-west-2 az-3)

Hi Marcus / Lauren,

We confirmed intermittent network flaps affecting us-west-2 az-3 between 08:30 - 09:25 PST. Traffic was briefly routed away by AWS LB, explaining the cross-region shift you observed. There were no hardware failures, but a transient control-plane event caused a burst of connection resets.

Recommended steps we applied with your permission:
- Short circuit traffic for OrbitAI away from az-3 until 14:00 PST.
- Ensured backend NLB connection timeouts were extended to reduce premature resets.

We will provide an incident summary and the control-plane event id by EOD. For long-term resilience, consider expanding multi-AZ active pools or adding regional edge caching for hot prefixes.

—Sandeep Rao
CloudIntegrate, Partner Support
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: nina@orbitai.com, ops@orbitai.com
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Executive escalation: OrbitAI impact & proposed customer remediation

Team — quick executive note for visibility.

What happened: us-west-2 az-3 experienced transient network flaps that caused substantial cross-region failover and a subsequent spike in latency and 5xxs for OrbitAI customers between ~08:45-09:40 PST. We implemented routing changes and temporary capacity increases; metrics show service largely stabilized by 10:10 PST.

Customer impact: OrbitAI reports session drops and degraded user experience during a critical launch window. This is a strategic account (ORB-4523).

Proposed remediation — please approve: 
1) Goodwill credit: 25% service credit for February invoice (approx. $12k).
2) Offer a free one-week dedicated capacity bump to cover their upcoming launch (no charge).
3) Schedule a joint postmortem with OrbitAI + CloudIntegrate + Redwood (proposed slot 2026-02-17 10:00 PST).

Requesting Evelyn / leadership sign-off on the credit and the proposed external postmortem. Sean — please prepare the customer note and include the timeline/what-we-did doc (I'll attach).

—Lauren
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: nina@orbitai.com, ops@orbitai.com
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T17:42:00-08:00
Subject: OrbitAI incident wrap + next steps (postmortem and action items)

Nina / team — final update and tracked actions from our side. Thanks for the patience while we stabilized traffic.

What we did (timeline):
- 08:45 PST: OrbitAI telemetry shows abrupt p95 jump.
- 09:10 PST: Auto-failover to us-east-1 observed; error rate increased.
- 09:52 PST: Redwood routing policy updated (force-route to us-east-1 / increased capacity).
- 10:10 PST: Observable service metrics returned toward baseline; no sustained errors after 10:25 PST.

Deliverables & next steps:
- Redwood to send formal incident report (postmortem-draft.md) by EOD 2/16.
- Joint postmortem on 2/17 10:00 PST (calendar invite: https://calendar.redwood.ai/event/pm-review-20260217).
- Credit applied: 25% off Feb invoice (pending leadership approval).
- Engineering action items: add regional edge cache for hot prefixes; evaluate multi-AZ active pool for OrbitAI. Marcus owns infra changes; ETA: 2/28.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md, latency-snapshot-20260214.png, traffic-metrics-20260214.csv

Thanks — we’ll keep the channel open for any follow-ups.

—Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
